llm.summary: This is a straightforward SMTP email-sending skill, but users should treat outgoing email content, attachments, and stored SMTP passwords carefully.

dimensions.detail: Read, write, and exec access is broad but coherent for creating a config file, reading an explicitly chosen attachment, and running a mail sender command; no automatic or unrelated use is described.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact is a single SKILL.md file with no bundled executable scripts, install hooks, or hidden setup behavior.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill clearly describes recipient, subject, body, attachment, and SMTP-provider use, but it should more prominently remind users that email bodies and attachments leave the local environment.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill instructs users to store SMTP credentials in email_config.json, including a password/app password; this is purpose-aligned but needs careful local secret handling.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The documented capabilities match the stated purpose: configuring SMTP, sending plain-text emails, optionally attaching one file, and testing Gmail or Outlook SMTP credentials.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, confirm you are comfortable with the agent sending selected message text and attachments through an external SMTP provider. Use an app-specific password or low-privilege sending account, keep email_config.json out of version control and shared folders, restrict file permissions, and verify recipients and attachments before sending.
llm.findings:
[SQP-2] expected: Sending recipient addresses, message bodies, and attachments to Gmail or Outlook SMTP servers is inherent to the skill's email-sending purpose, though the disclosure could be clearer.
[SQP-2] expected: A local SMTP credential file is disclosed and purpose-aligned, but plaintext password storage should be treated as a security hygiene risk rather than hidden or malicious behavior.
